- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model often overcorrects downward — adjust upward to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast growth after 2–3 days of spike.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in the 30-day horizon — add 2–5% buffer to forecast if recent 7-day average is rising.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag — forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment turning point.  
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline after peak), model often holds too high — reduce forecast by 1–3% per day of reversion.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model often drifts toward historical mean — adjust forecast to align with recent 14-day moving average.
